neighbours.label: a preposition repeated in an elliptical parallel after 'as', 'i.e.' or 'than' ('spoke of her as of a saint', 'applies to adults, i.e., to anyone over 18'); the same sentence without the repeated preposition stays low
fire: He always spoke of his teacher as of a saint who could do no wrong.
The new rule applies to adults, i.e., to anyone over eighteen.
They prepared for the inspection as for a siege, stocking every shelf.
She wrote about the war as about a distant dream.
The grant is limited to the coastal towns, i.e., to the villages near the sea.
He longed for the city as for a lost love.
We think of the old mill as of a member of the family.
The tax falls on the poorest households, i.e., on families with no savings.

notes: Card peaks ' to'/' of'/' de'/' for' right after 'as', 'i.e.,', 'que', 'wie': 'fell at the battle ... as of men that were punished', 'stipulate for them as for aliens', 'to the micro-political one, i.e., to an analysis'. Probe: only the true repeat fired: 'to the local one, i.e., to an analysis' 0.411; 'as of no more worth' (no repeat) 0.028, 'as for minors' without an earlier 'for' 0.045, 'so to speak' 0.035, 'such as the iPad' 0.044. Hypothesis: the preposition is a parallel copy of an earlier one.
